::: {.landing-bio}
I'm a health economist and Associate Professor at the Yale School of Public Health. I'm also a Faculty Research Fellow at the National Bureau of Economic Research and an Affiliated Professor at J-PAL.

I discovered my interest in Medicaid before I knew anything about health economics. After college, I spent three years working on Medicaid policy for New York State. During my time there we were continually implementing new policies and programs, but rarely had time to look in the rearview mirror to see whether they were working. That experience ultimately led me to economics and left me with many of the questions I still wrestle with in my research.

Today, I study the economics of public insurance programs. Much of my work focuses on Medicaid: what difference a health plan makes, how insurers’ decisions shape the care people receive, and how states can make better use of limited resources. I use randomized and quasi-experimental designs, often in close partnership with state agencies. Many of my research questions come from conversations with the people running social insurance programs.

My research has appeared in leading economics and clinical journals including the *American Economic Review* and the *New England Journal of Medicine*, and received the 
Willard G. Manning Award for the Best Research in Health Econometrics and the American Statistical Association's Outstanding Statistical 
Application Award. It has also been widely covered by the media, including the *New York Times*, *Washington Post*, and *NPR*.

Before academia, I also worked as a data scientist in Silicon Valley and co-founded Young Invincibles, an advocacy organization for young adults. I earned my undergraduate degree at Swarthmore College and my PhD at Harvard University.

:::
:::


## Recent research

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
feat <- yaml::read_yaml("data/featured.yml")
esc <- function(x) gsub("<", "&lt;", gsub("&", "&amp;", x, fixed = TRUE), fixed = TRUE)
cat('<div class="featured">\n')
for (f in feat) cat(sprintf(
  '<div class="feature"><img src="%s" alt="Figure from %s" loading="lazy"><div class="feature-body"><div class="feature-label">%s</div><div class="feature-title"><a href="%s">%s</a></div><div class="feature-finding">%s</div></div></div>\n',
  f$image, esc(f$title), esc(f$label), f$url, esc(f$title), esc(f$finding)))
cat('</div>\n\n<p class="feature-more"><a href="research.qmd">All research &rarr;</a></p>\n')
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
source("R/substack.R")
posts <- yaml::read_yaml("data/substack_posts.yml")
if (length(posts) > 0) {
  cat("## Latest writing\n\n")
  for (p in head(posts, 3)) {
    cat(sprintf(
      '<div class="post"><div class="meta">%s · %s</div><div class="headline"><a href="%s">%s</a></div></div>\n',
      html_escape(p$date), toupper(p$source), html_escape(p$url), html_escape(p$title)))
  }
  cat('\n[All writing →](writing.qmd)\n')
}
```
